messages.subject: switched alleles & multiple linkage groups
parts:
What is the cause of switched alleles?

Is this just a matter of miscalling genotypes or are there other sources of this problem?


I took the first 9 linkage groups from the rqtl analysis and have been able to assign them to the organism’s 3 chromosomes.

The manual mentions that if there are a lot of switched alleles, one may recover multiple linkage groups for one chromosome but that does not appear to be my case as when I ran checkAlleles, only detected 1 marker.


Could it just be there is a big gap between the markers?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] switched alleles & multiple linkage groups
parts:
Yes; in my experience, these switched alleles are due to genotyping errors.

The software looks for pairs of markers with associated genotypes (large LOD score for testing that the recombination fraction between them is not equal to 1/2), but with estimated recombination fraction > 1/2. (Near 1 rather than near 0.)

Gaps between markers should lead to rf ~ 1/2 and LOD ~ 0.

karl
